version: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology — Supportive Care
source: NCCN Guidelines v2.2024 — Antiemesis, Fever and Neutropenia, Cancer-Related Fatigue, Adult Cancer Pain

EMERGENCY.label: EMERGENCY
EMERGENCY.action: Call 911 or go to the nearest Emergency Department immediately. Do NOT wait for a clinic appointment.

URGENT.label: URGENT
URGENT.action: Contact your oncology team or nurse line NOW. Same-day evaluation required.

ROUTINE.label: ROUTINE
ROUTINE.action: Schedule an appointment with your oncology team within 24-48 hours.

SELF_CARE.label: SELF-CARE
SELF_CARE.action: Manage at home with the following guidance. Monitor for worsening. Call if symptoms escalate.

rules.name: Febrile Neutropenia — Single High Fever
rules.guideline: NCCN Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-Related Infections v2.2024
rules.citation: NCCN Guidelines v2.2024; Freifeld AG et al. CID 2011;52:e56-e93
rules.reasoning_template: Temperature {temp}°C meets NCCN febrile neutropenia threshold (≥38.3°C single reading). Last chemotherapy {chemo_days} days ago (within 14-day neutropenic window). Immediate ED evaluation required — blood cultures, CBC with differential, and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics per NCCN FN protocol.

rules.name: Febrile Neutropenia — Sustained Fever
rules.guideline: NCCN Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-Related Infections v2.2024
rules.reasoning_template: Temperature {temp}°C sustained for ≥1 hour meets alternate NCCN febrile neutropenia criterion. Last chemotherapy {chemo_days} days ago. Emergency evaluation required.

rules.name: Dyspnea at Rest
rules.citation: CTCAE v5.0 Grade 3 Dyspnea; NCCN Survivorship v2.2024
rules.reasoning_template: Dyspnea at rest (CTCAE Grade ≥3) is a life-threatening emergency in oncology patients. Possible etiologies include pulmonary embolism, pleural effusion, cardiac tamponade, or pneumonitis. Immediate emergency evaluation required.

rules.name: Neurologic Red Flags
rules.guideline: NCCN Central Nervous System Cancers; NCCN Survivorship
rules.reasoning_template: New neurologic symptoms ({symptoms}) in an oncology patient require emergency evaluation to rule out brain metastasis, leptomeningeal disease, stroke, or cord compression. Immediate imaging required.

rules.name: Bleeding with Thrombocytopenia History
rules.reasoning_template: Any bleeding in a patient with thrombocytopenia history requires urgent evaluation. Platelet count may be critically low. Transfusion support and oncology assessment needed same day.

rules.name: Grade 3+ Bleeding
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} bleeding (CTCAE v5.0) — transfusion or operative intervention may be required. Emergency evaluation required.

rules.name: Dehydration Risk — Severe Vomiting
rules.citation: NCCN Antiemesis v2.2024; Roila F et al. Ann Oncol 2016
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} vomiting (≥6 episodes/24h, CTCAE v5.0) carries significant dehydration risk. IV hydration, antiemetic escalation, and electrolyte assessment required on a same-day basis.

rules.name: Dehydration Risk — Severe Diarrhea
rules.citation: NCCN Survivorship v2.2024; Benson AB et al. J Clin Oncol 2004
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} diarrhea (≥7 stools/day above baseline, CTCAE v5.0) requires urgent assessment for dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, and possible infectious etiology (C. difficile). Same-day evaluation required.

rules.name: Uncontrolled Severe Pain
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} pain (NRS {nrs}/10, CTCAE v5.0) unresponsive to current analgesic regimen. Per NCCN Adult Cancer Pain guidelines, dose titration and reassessment required same day. Consider IV/SC opioid rotation.

rules.name: Severe Uncontrolled Pain (Grade 4)
rules.reasoning_template: Grade 4 pain (NRS 10/10, CTCAE v5.0) — disabling, unable to perform self-care. Emergency pain management required. Rule out new oncologic emergency (cord compression, pathologic fracture, organ obstruction).

rules.name: Constipation — Suspected Obstruction
rules.reasoning_template: Grade 4 constipation with obstipation — possible bowel obstruction in oncology patient. Emergency surgical evaluation required.

rules.name: Severe Mucositis — Unable to Swallow
rules.guideline: NCCN Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-Related Infections
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} oral mucositis (CTCAE v5.0) — severe pain interfering with oral intake. Nutritional support, aggressive pain management, and infection prophylaxis review required. Same-day evaluation.

rules.name: Worsening Peripheral Neuropathy
rules.citation: NCCN Survivorship v2.2024; Loprinzi CL et al.
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} peripheral neuropathy (CTCAE v5.0) limiting self-care ADLs. Per NCCN CIPN guidelines, dose modification of neurotoxic chemotherapy and neurology referral should be considered. Schedule within 24-48 hours.

rules.name: Severe Cancer-Related Fatigue
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} fatigue (CTCAE v5.0) not relieved by rest, limiting self-care ADLs. NCCN recommends screening for treatable contributing factors: anemia (CBC), hypothyroidism (TSH), depression (PHQ-9), sleep disturbance. Schedule within 24-48 hours.

rules.name: Fever Without Recent Chemo
rules.reasoning_template: Grade {grade} fever ({temp}°C) in oncology patient without recent chemotherapy. Infectious workup required — consider immunosuppression from steroids, biologic agents, or disease-related immunodeficiency.
